title: Opening the Turing Lock
description: Simulate a simple two-register computer with halve, triple, increment, and conditional jump instructions.
writeup:
## Approach

Straightforward instruction interpreter. Parse each line into an opcode and arguments, then step through with a program counter.

## Part 1

The six instructions map directly to simple operations: `hlf`, `tpl`, and `inc` modify a register and advance PC by 1; `jmp` jumps unconditionally; `jie` and `jio` jump conditionally (if even, if one). The program halts when PC goes out of bounds. We run with `a=0, b=0` and return the final value of `b`.

## Part 2

Same program, but register `a` starts at 1. The program is essentially computing a Collatz-like sequence — starting with a higher value of `a` produces a much longer computation and a larger final `b`.
